answer: Each agent identity must post its own refundable stake and burn a small on-chain fee before attesting, and a cap limits how many identities one funding source may stake. An attacker cannot farm free clones, since every fake agent locks real capital first. Cohorts sharing funding ancestry are grouped, so a hundred clones carry one node's weight. Attack cost climbs in a spiral as clones rise while voting weight stays flat, so a takeover costs more than honest mining. Validators flag clusters and slash stakes at the dawn of detection, turning each lost stake into a lantern lit only as a warning.
